semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {الذين يُكَذِّبُونَ}: it may follow [the preceding noun] (itbāʿ) as a naʿt (adjective), a badal (substitute) or a bayān (explicative apposition), or it may be cut off (qaṭʿ), in the nominative or the accusative.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {إِذَا}: the majority read it as a statement. Al-Ḥasan read «أإذا» as a disapproving (inkārī) question. The majority read «تُتْلى» with two dotted-above tāʾs, while Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Miqsam read it with the yāʾ dotted below, because the feminine gender is metaphorical (majāzī).

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {بَلْ رَانَ}: Ḥafṣ's pause on «بل» was discussed earlier in al-Kahf. Al-rayn and al-rān are a covering over the heart, like rust on a polished thing such as a sword, a mirror and the like. The poet said:
4515 - وكم رانَ مِنْ ذنبٍ على قلبِ فاجِرٍ ... فتابَ مِن الذنبِ الذي ران وانْجَلَى
(How many a sin has covered the heart of a sinner, and then he repented of the sin that covered it, and it cleared away.)
The original meaning of al-rayn is overpowering (al-ghalaba); from it comes: "the wine overpowered (rānat) the mind of its drinker", and "the swoon overpowered the mind of the sick man". The poet said:
4516 -. . . . . . . . . . . . رانَتْ به الخَمْ ... رُ. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(… the wine overpowered him …)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "One says: rāna ʿalayhi al-dhanbu and ghāna [the sin covered him], with the maṣdars (verbal nouns) raynan and ghaynan. Al-ghayn is cloud (al-ghaym). One says: rāna fīhi al-nawm, i.e. sleep became firmly settled in him; and rānat bihi al-khamr, i.e. the wine carried him off." Abū Zayd reported: "rīna bi-l-rajuli raynan [the man was overcome]", so its maṣdar comes with the middle radical both with fatḥa and with sukūn. And «ما كانوا» is the fāʿil (agent). «ما» may be maṣdariyya, or it may mean "that which" (alladhī), with the returning pronoun omitted. The alif of «ران» was read both with imāla (inclination) and with tafkhīm (full a-sound): the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Abū Bakr read it with imāla, and the rest with tafkhīm. The lām of «بل» was both assimilated into the rāʾ and pronounced distinctly.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {عَن رَّبِّهِمْ}: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the khabar (predicate), and so is «يومئذٍ». The tanwīn [in يومئذ] compensates for a clause whose implied form is: "on the day when people stand", because nothing else would fit as its implied form.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {يُقَالُ}: what stands in place of the agent [i.e. the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)] may be what is indicated by the clause in his saying {هذا الذي كُنتُمْ}; it may be the clause itself; and it may be the maṣdar (verbal noun). This was set out in detail at the beginning of al-Baqara.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {لَفِي عِلِّيِّينَ}: it is the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said here just what he said there, and he is answered with what was said before. ʿIlliyyūn is the plural of ʿilliyy, or it is the name of a place in the highest part of Paradise, and it has been treated like the plural of rational beings, so it takes wāw in the nominative and yāʾ in the accusative and genitive, although the condition of rationality is not met. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Its singular is ʿilliyy, which is the angel. It has also been said: it is a plural form like ʿishrūn (twenty)"; then he mentioned something similar to what he mentioned regarding «سِجِّين» concerning the omission mentioned before. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "ʿIlliyyūn is a proper name (ʿalam) for the register of good in which is recorded everything that the angels and the righteous among humans and jinn have done; it is transferred from the plural of ʿilliyy, of the pattern fiʿʿīl from al-ʿuluww (height), like «سِجِّين» from al-sijn (prison). It was so named either because it is the cause of elevation, or because it is raised up in the seventh heaven." I say: all the views given earlier on «سِجِّين» apply here as well.

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {يَشْهَدُهُ}: a clause which may be a second ṣifa (adjective), or may be resumptive (mustaʾnafa).

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {تَعْرِفُ}: the majority read it with the verb ascribed to the one addressed, i.e. "you recognise", O Muhammad, or anyone capable of recognising.
Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Shayba, Ṭalḥa, Yaʿqūb and al-Zaʿfarānī read «تُعْرَفُ» in the passive, with «نَضْرَةُ» in the nominative as standing in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil). ʿAlī ibn Zayd read likewise, except with the yāʾ below, because the feminine gender is metaphorical.
[And his saying {يَنظُرُونَ} is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in the khabar, or it is resumptive.] [And «على الأرائك» is attached to «يَنْظرون», or is a ḥāl from its pronoun, or is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the khabar.]

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {مِن رَّحِيقٍ}: al-raḥīq is a drink in which there is no adulteration; it has also been said: the finest wine. Ḥassān said:
4517 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... بَرَدى يُصَفِّقُ بالرَّحيقِ السَّلْسَلِ
(… [the water of] Baradā mixed with pure, smooth-flowing wine.)

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying: {خِتَامُهُ}: al-Kisāʾī read «خاتَمهُ», with fatḥa on the tāʾ after the alif; the rest read it with the tāʾ before the alif. The rationale of al-Kisāʾī's reading is that he made it a noun for that with which the cup is sealed, as shown by his saying «مَخْتوم» (sealed); then He made clear what the seal is. It is also reported from al-Kisāʾī that he read the tāʾ with kasra, so it would be like the saying of the Exalted: {وَخَاتَمَ النبيين} [al-Aḥzāb: 40]; the meaning is: a seal whose scent is musk. The rationale of the reading of the majority is that al-khitām is the clay with which a thing is sealed, and musk was put in its place. The poet said:
4518 - كأنَّ مُشَعْشَعاً مِنْ خَمْرِ بُصْرى ... . . . . . . البُخْتُ مَسْدودَ الخِتامِ
(As if diluted wine of Buṣrā … the Bactrian camels [carried], its seal stopped up.)
It has also been said: [khitām is] its blend and its mixture. It has also been said: its ending, i.e. the end of drinking it, in which a person finds the scent of musk. Al-tanāfus (vying) is contending for a precious (nafīs) thing. One says: nafistu bihi nafāsatan, i.e. I was miserly with it. Its origin is from al-nafs (the soul), because of its preciousness.

semin-durr:27-27.t: His saying: {مِن تَسْنِيمٍ}: tasnīm is the name of a spring in Paradise. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Tasnīm is a proper name (ʿalam) for a particular spring, named with tasnīm, which is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of sanamahu, when one raises it." I say: there is a difficulty in this, because it ought then to have been a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) owing to being a proper name and feminine, even if the feminine is metaphorical. Its being masculine in origin does not detract from that, because what counts is its state as a proper name: do you not see that they state explicitly that if a woman were named Zayd it would have to be a diptote, even though in «هِنْد» there are two options? Unless you say: it was treated in the manner of Hind and the like, so it would be like Wāsiṭ and Dābiq.

semin-durr:28-28.t: His saying: {عَيْناً}: there are several views on it. First: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial); al-Zajjāj said this, meaning from «تَسْنيم», because it is a proper name for a particular thing — except that it is problematic because it is a non-derived (jāmid) noun. Second: it is accusative by way of praise; al-Zamakhsharī said this. Third: it is accusative through an implied «يُسْقَونْ» (they are given to drink); al-Akhfash said this. As for his saying «يَشْرب» بها: i.e. from it; or the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); or «يَشْربُ» is made to include the meaning of "to quench one's thirst" (yarwī). This was discussed fully in Sūrat al-Insān.

semin-durr:29-29.t: His saying: {َمِنَ الذين آمَنُواْ}: attached to «يَضْحكون», i.e. on account of them; it was put first for the sake of the verse-endings (fawāṣil). Al-taghāmuz is signalling with the eye.

semin-durr:31-31.t: His saying: {فَكِهِينَ}: Ḥafṣ read «فَكِهين» without an alif, and the rest with it. It has been said: the two have the same meaning. It has also been said: fakihīn means insolent, and fākihīn is from al-tafakkuh (jesting). It has also been said: fakihīn means rejoicing, and fākihīn means living in comfort. It has also been said: fākihīn means people of fruit and jest.

semin-durr:32-32.t: His saying: {وَإِذَا رَأَوْهُمْ}: the nominative [pronoun] may refer to the disbelievers and the accusative one to the believers, and the reverse is also possible; and likewise the two pronouns in «أُرْسِلوا عليهم».

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {فاليوم}: accusative through «يَضْحَكون». Its being placed before the mubtadaʾ (subject) does no harm, because if the governing word were placed first here it would be permissible, since there is no ambiguity — unlike «زيدٌ قام في الدار», for which one may not say: في الدار زيدٌ قام.

semin-durr:35-35.t: His saying: {عَلَى الأرآئك يَنظُرُونَ}: as was said on its parallel.

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying: {هَلْ ثُوِّبَ}: the interrogative clause may suspend (tuʿalliq) the "looking" before it, so it would be in the position of the accusative after the preposition is dropped. It may also be on the implication of an omitted verb of saying, i.e. "they say: have [the disbelievers] been repaid?". Thuwwiba means: was recompensed. One says: thawwabahu and athābahu. The poet said:
4519 - سَأَجْزِيك أو يَجْزيك عني مُثَوِّبٌ ... وحَسْبُك أَنْ يُثْنَى عليك وتُحْمَدَا
(I shall repay you, or a rewarder will repay you on my behalf; and it is enough for you to be praised and lauded.)
Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza assimilated the lām of «هل» into the thāʾ. In his saying «ما كانوا» there is an omission, i.e. "the reward of what they used to [do]". And «ما» is a nominal relative or a particle relative (i.e. maṣdariyya).

semin-durr:9-9.t:
Al-raqm means writing (al-khaṭṭ). It has also been said: sealing (al-khatm), in the dialect of Ḥimyar; but the first is correct. The poet said:
4514 - سأَرْقُمُ في الماءِ القَراح إليكُمُ ... على بُعْدِكُمْ إنْ كان للماءِ راقِمُ
(I shall write to you on clear water, despite your distance, if water could ever be written upon.)
This root was discussed earlier in al-Kahf.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {وَيْلٌ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject); what justified beginning with it [though indefinite] is its being an imprecation. Had it been accusative, it would have been permissible. Makkī said: "The preferred form for «وَيْل» and the like, when not in iḍāfa (genitive construct), is the nominative, and the accusative is permissible. If it is in iḍāfa or made definite, the preferred form / is the accusative, as in {وَيْلَكُمْ لاَ تَفْتَرُواْ} [Ṭā Hā: 61]." «للمُطَفِّفين» is its khabar (predicate).
Al-muṭaffif is the one who gives short measure. Its real meaning is taking, in measure or weight, something ṭafīf, i.e. scanty and paltry; from it is their saying "below the ṭafīf", i.e. the trifling thing, because of its smallness.

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {عَلَى الناس}: There are several views concerning it. The first: that it is attached to «اكْتالوا», «على» and «مِنْ» alternating here. Al-Farrāʾ said: "One says iktaltu ʿalā al-nās: I took full measure from them; and iktaltu minhum: I took what they owed." It was also said: «على» means «مِنْ»; one says iktaltu ʿalayhi and minhu with one meaning; but the first is clearer. It was also said: «على» is attached to «يَسْتَوْفُون». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Since their taking by measure was a taking by measure that harmed [the people] and in which [the people] were wronged, He put «على» in place of «مِنْ» to indicate that. It may also be attached to «يَسْتَوْفون», the object being placed before the verb to convey specificity, i.e. they take full measure against people specifically; as for themselves, they take full measure for them." End of quotation. And it is good.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {كَالُوهُمْ أَوْ وَّزَنُوهُمْ}: They were written in the codex without an alif after the wāw in both verbs; for this reason people disagreed about «هم» in two ways. The first: it is an accusative pronoun, so it is a direct object and refers to the people, i.e. when they measure for the people or weigh for the people. On this view these two verbs in origin take two objects, one directly without disagreement and the other by means of a preposition, which may be deleted. Whether each of the two [constructions] is original in itself, or one of them is the origin of the other, is a well-known disagreement. The implied form is: when they measure food for them or weigh it for them; then the preposition and the free object were deleted. Al-Zamakhsharī recited:
4513 - ولقد جَنَيْتُكَ أَكْمُؤاً وعَساقِلاً ... ولقد نَهْيْتُك عَن بناتِ الأَوْبَرِ
(I have gathered you truffles and white truffles, and I have forbidden you the inferior small truffles.)
i.e. gathered for you. The second: that it is a nominative pronoun emphasising the wāw, the pronoun referring to the defrauders; on this view the thing measured and the one for whom it is measured, and the thing weighed and the one for whom it is weighed, have all been omitted. However, al-Zamakhsharī rejected this and said: "It is not valid for it to be a nominative pronoun for the defrauders, because the speech would thereby turn into a corrupt arrangement. That is, the meaning is: when they take from people they take in full, and when they give to them they cause loss. If you make the pronoun refer to the defrauders, it turns into your saying: when they take from people they take in full, and when they themselves in particular undertake the measuring or weighing they cause loss; and this is incoherent speech, because the discourse is about the act, not about the one performing it."
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "There is no incoherence in it in any way, and there is no difference between emphasising the pronoun or not; the discourse is about the act. The most that is in this is that what taking in full is attached to, namely «على الناس», is mentioned, while in {كَالُوهُمْ أَوْ وَّزَنُوهُمْ} it is omitted because it is known, since it is known that they do not cause loss to themselves." I say: al-Zamakhsharī wants to preserve that the meaning is tied to two things: when they take from others, and when they give to others; and this is complete only on the supposition that the pronoun is accusative referring to the people, not that it is a nominative pronoun referring to the defrauders. There is no doubt that this meaning which al-Zamakhsharī mentioned and intended is more complete and better than the second meaning. The first is preferred by the absence of the alif after the wāw, since that indicates the pronoun's being attached. However, al-Zamakhsharī made a qualification, saying: "Relying, in invalidating it, on the script of the codex and on the alif written after the wāw of the plural not being present in it is feeble, because the script of the codex in much of it did not observe the norm agreed upon in the science of writing. Besides, I have seen in books written by the hands of meticulous imams this alif rejected, because it has no reality in either pronunciation or meaning, since the wāw alone gives the meaning of the plural. This alif was written only to distinguish between the wāw of the plural and others in forms like your saying «هم [لم] يَدْعُوا» and «هو يَدْعُو»; whoever did not write it said: the meaning suffices to distinguish between them. It is reported from ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Ḥamza that they adopted that, i.e. they made the two pronouns refer to the defrauders, and paused at the two wāws a slight pause by which they made clear what they intended."
He did not mention the act of weighing first; rather, He restricted Himself to measuring and said «إذا اكْتالوا», and did not say "or took by weight", as He said the second time «أو وَزَنُوهم». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is as though the defrauders used to take what is measured and weighed only by measures, not by scales, because by taking by measure they were able to take in full and to steal, since they would shake [the measure] and use tricks in filling it; and when they gave, / they measured and weighed, because they were able to cheat in both kinds."
His saying «يُخْسِرون» is the apodosis (jawāb) of «إذا», and it is made transitive by the hamza. One says: the man khasira (lost), and I akhsartuhu (made him lose); so its object is omitted, i.e. they make people lose their goods.

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {أَلا يَظُنُّ}: The apparent view is that it is the «ألا» of urging (taḥḍīḍ): He urged them to that, and «الظنّ» then means certainty. It was also said: it is the negating «لا» with the interrogative hamza entering it.

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ يَقُومُ}: It may be accusative by «مَبْعُوثون», as al-Zamakhsharī said; or by an implied «يُبْعَثون»; or as a badal (substitute) for the position of «يوم»; or by an implied «أَعْني»; or it is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject); or genitive as a badal for «ليومٍ عظيمٍ». In these last two aspects it was only made indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because of its iḍāfa (genitive construct) to the verb, even though [the verb] is imperfect, as is the view of the Kufans. What indicates the soundness of these two aspects is the reading of Zayd ibn ʿAlī «يومُ يقومُ» in the nominative, and what Abū Muʿādh the reader related: «يوم» in the genitive, according to what has preceded.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {لَفِي سِجِّينٍ}: They disagreed about the nūn of «سِجِّين». It was said: it is radical; its derivation is from al-sijn, which is imprisonment, and it is an intensive form; so sijjīn is from al-sajn as sikkīr is from al-sukr. It was also said: rather, it is a replacement for lām, the origin being sijjīl, derived from al-sijill, which is a written record. They also disagreed about it: is it the name of a place or the name of a specific book? And is it an adjective, or a proper name transferred from an adjective, like Ḥātim? It is fully declinable (maṣrūf), since there is only one cause [of diptosis] in it, namely being a proper name. If it is the name of a place, then His saying «كتابٌ مَرْقُوْمٌ» is either a badal (substitute) for it, or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), which is a pronoun referring to it. On both assumptions it is problematic, because the book is not the place. So it was said: the implied form is "it is the place of a book", and then the muḍāf was deleted. It was also said: the implied form is "And what will make you know what the book of sijjīn is?" So the deletion is either from the first or from the second. If, however, we say that it is the name of a book, there is no problem.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Whoever says that sijjīn is a place, then «كتابٌ» is nominative as the khabar of «إنّ», and the adverbial phrase «لفي سِجِّين» is non-operative (mulghā); and whoever makes it an expression for loss, then «كتابٌ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied form being 'it is a book', and this speech explains what sijjīn is." End of quotation. This is not valid at all, since the entry of the lām determines that it is the khabar, so it cannot be non-operative. It cannot be said: the lām enters what the khabar governs, and this is of that kind, so it is non-operative; because if the khabar, namely «كتابٌ», were supposed to govern, or its adjective «مرقوم» to govern, that would be impossible. As for «كتابٌ» being prevented from governing, it is because it is qualified, and a qualified maṣdar (verbal noun) does not govern. As for «مرقومٌ» being prevented from governing, it is because it is an adjective, and what an adjective governs does not precede the noun it qualifies. Moreover, the lām enters what the khabar governs only under its condition, and this is not governed by the khabar. So it is determined that the preposition-phrase is the khabar and is not non-operative. As for his second statement, "and this speech explains what sijjīn is", it is problematic, because the book is not the loss to which the pronoun was made to refer, being informed about by «كتابٌ».
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: Allah the Exalted has informed about the book of the wicked that it is in sijjīn, and has explained sijjīn by «كتاب مرقوم», so it is as though it were said: their book is in a written book—what then is its meaning? I say: «سِجِّين» is a comprehensive book; it is the register of evil in which Allah has recorded the deeds of the devils and the deeds of the unbelievers and the wicked among jinn and men. It is a book inscribed, clear in its writing, or marked, so that whoever sees it knows that there is no good in it. So the meaning is that what is written of the deeds of the wicked is recorded in that register. It is called sijjīl «[Translator's note: so in the text; the context indicates «سِجِّيناً» (sijjīn)]», of the pattern fiʿʿīl, from al-sajl «[Translator's note: so in the text; the context indicates «السَّجْن» (al-sajn)]», which is imprisonment and constriction, because it is the cause of imprisonment and constriction in Hell." End of quotation.
